thesis: The speaker argues that emerging market funds historically underperform because they enter markets only after insiders have already profited and prices have risen significantly. He posits that successful investing in these markets requires acting like a private trader by getting in early, often through local brokerages, rather than waiting for established custody arrangements or global depositary receipts.
